articles.title: Bears Beat Panthers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Caleb Williams, Young, Odunze & Top Players
articles.summary: Caleb Williams led the Chicago Bears to a 59-37 victory over Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, opening their season with a winning record.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams led the Chicago Bears to a 59-37 victory over Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, opening their season with a winning record.

Despite being the home team, the Panthers were a 2.5-point underdog heading into the matchup, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

There was no defense in sight as a combined 96 points and 1,030 yards were put up in the season opener at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte.

Despite kicking off the game with a fumble for a loss, Chicago made up for it by finding the end zone twice in the first quarter. Williams ran it in for a 9-yard touchdown, and D'Andre Swift capped off a 67-yard drive with a short run up the middle to score.

Off the Bears' opening fumble, Young and the Panthers charged 42 yards downfield, capping off the drive with a 4-yard connection to Chuba Hubbard. Despite the defensive stop and early strike, Chicago led 14-7 after one quarter.

Williams connected with Cole Kmet for a 22-yard touchdown to open the second quarter. After going three-and-out on its next possession, a muffed punt was recovered by Chicago and turned into three points with a successful field goal.

Williams showed how good he is on his feet, scrambling for 29 yards to score once more.

Carolina scored on three of its five possessions, adding a deep 51-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Coker and a 7-yard touchdown run by Young before closing out with a field goal.

With 15 minutes left to play, the Bears led 45-31 in an insanely high-scoring Week 1 game.

Panthers' Hubbard added another score on a short, 2-yard run to tie it at 31-apiece before Chicago's Swift ran one up the middle for another score in the third, while Kyle Monangai broke loose for a 61-yard touchdown run.

Chicago began to pull away in the fourth, adding two touchdowns — a short pass to Jahdae Walker and another Swift run, his third of the day.

The Panthers opened the quarter with a fumble but found a touchdown on their next drive with another Young-Coker connection. Time ran out, and Chicago's late pullaway was too much to overcome.

Chicago will look to keep its hot offensive prowess going against the Minnesota Vikings next Sunday, while Carolina will hit the road to face the Atlanta Falcons. Both games are scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza's Mom Talks Raiders QB's Tom Brady Relationship & 'Open Line of Communication'
articles.summary: Elsa Mendoza, the mother of Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, has been impressed with the team's minority owner, Tom Brady, and thankful for the relationship he's fostered with her son.
articles.body:
Elsa Mendoza, the mother of Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, has been impressed with the team's minority owner, Tom Brady, and thankful for the relationship he's fostered with her son.

"He's such a kind person, and he's everything you would expect and more," she told People's Skyler Caruso regarding Brady. "You would think that, being everything he's accomplished and all the records he's broken, that he would be somebody untouchable. He is so kind. He has always made us feel like the door's open. Anytime we need him to call, he's been so welcoming to Fernando, helps Fernando with any questions, tells Fernando there's an open line of communication. He's also offered that to us. I mean, I could not want a better mentor for my son. He is a kind person, a good person, an excellent football player."

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

The Raiders have opted to start the season with Kirk Cousins as the first-team quarterback, allowing Mendoza time to learn the offense and adjust to life in the NFL. Brady can relate—he spent his entire first season in New England behind Drew Bledsoe on the depth chart before being called into action in his second season due to a Bledsoe injury (and the rest, of course, is history).

Granted, Brady was famously a sixth-round pick, while Mendoza was the top overall selection in April's draft. But the Raiders never made it a secret they intended to bring along Mendoza—or any young quarterback—slowly.

"Ideally, you don't want [a rookie QB] to start from Day 1," Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters in early April, before Mendoza was even selected. "You'd love him to be able to learn behind somebody. That's in a perfect world. It doesn't always work out that way. Sometimes they have to play from Day 1, and it's our job as coaches to get them ready to go. I think it does help the player if they can sit behind a mature adult and watch how they run the show."

Having a future first-ballot Hall of Famer serving as a mentor doesn't hurt either.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo 'Cleared for Flipping' After Trending Celebration Video From Giants' Win vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo did a backflip after scoring a touchdown in his team's 28-20 season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday evening.
articles.body:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo did a backflip after scoring a touchdown in his team's 28-20 season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday evening.

Giants fans' hearts may have skipped some beats watching that considering Skattebo suffered right leg injuries (severe right ankle dislocation, broken fibula/tibia fracture and torn deltoid ligament) during a game against the Philadelphia Eagles last October .

However, as Skattebo told his social media followers, he has been "cleared for flipping."

Skattebo did quite well in his first full NFL game back from injury, rushing for 81 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries.

It's clear Skattebo has been cleared for flipping and full workloads, given how much he did Sunday. His tough running helped the Giants control the ball for 36 minutes and 40 seconds on Sunday. In fact, Dallas had the ball only twice in the second half.

Skattebo was the top pick in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL draft. He showed great promise in his rookie season, amassing 617 total yards and seven touchdowns in eight games.

Sadly, Skattebo's season ended prematurely, but he looks 100 percent now.

Skattebo did some offseason flips at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game in May and Fanatics Fest in July. Skattebo didn't land the July one cleanly, leading to a harrowing second or two, but he got up and appeared fine afterward.

Skattebo will hope to perform more end zone back flips on Monday when the Giants visit the Los Angeles Rams.

articles.title: Jordan Mason Injury Update, Latest on Vikings RB's Status and Fantasy Implications Before NFL Week 2
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings placed running back Jordan Mason on injured reserve due to a thumb injury, the team announced Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings placed running back Jordan Mason on injured reserve due to a thumb injury, the team announced Wednesday.

The Vikings also signed running back DeeJay Dallas to their active roster while adding running back Jerome Ford to their practice squad.

As for Mason, he'll now miss a minimum of four games before he'll be eligible to return.

From a fantasy football perspective, Aaron Jones is expected to receive the bulk of the available opportunities in Minnesota's backfield until Mason comes back.

It shouldn't be a lengthy absence, though.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters Wednesday that Mason suffered a small fracture in his thumb, but it had been fixed.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport also noted that Mason "should be back quickly."

The former Georgia Tech standout is beginning his second season in Minnesota after rushing for 758 yards and six touchdowns across 16 appearances throughout his 2025 campaign.

During the Vikings' 39-22 win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, Mason picked up 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 attempts. While it only represented an average of 3.9 yards per carry, it's worth noting that he faced at least eight defenders in the box on 20 percent of his opportunities (via Next Gen Stats ).

Mason also helped Minnesota complete a 12-point comeback in the second half against Green Bay with a 28-yard run in the fourth quarter.

The Vikings' first contest without Mason will take place against the Chicago Bears in Week 2. The Bears previously allowed 125 yards on the ground during their season-opening win over the Carolina Panthers.

Kickoff between Minnesota and Chicago is on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Ja'Kobi Lane Placed on IR, Latest Injury Updates, Return Timeline, Fantasy Outlook for Ravens WR
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane will miss at least four games after fracturing his wrist while making his NFL debut in Sunday's season-opening victory over the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane will miss at least four games after fracturing his wrist while making his NFL debut in Sunday's season-opening victory over the Indianapolis Colts.

Lane will be placed on injured reserve after undergoing successful surgery on Wednesday, coach Jesse Minter told reporters.

"Definitely have a really good chance of coming back here pretty quick, I would say," Minter said.

Minter also said Zay Flowers is "day to day" after suffering a hamstring injury Sunday.

Devontez Walker was inactive for Week 1, though he figures to get an extended look moving forward. The Ravens also have Rashod Bateman and LaJohntay Wester heading into a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Wednesday Lane "should be back around the time he's eligible to return."

Lane is currently scheduled to sit out games against the Saints, Dallas Cowboys, Tennessee Titans and Atlanta Falcons over the next month. He will be eligible to return for the Ravens' Week 6 matchup Oct. 18 at the Cleveland Browns.

The Ravens selected Lane in the third round of the 2026 draft. He earned buzz as a potential WR3 candidate during a strong training camp.

In a recent locker room poll by BaltimoreRavens.com's Ryan Mink and Quentin Corpuel , seven players named Lane as the team's most likely breakout player this season.

Lane was targeted three times in his NFL debut, making one catch for 11 yards before he was ruled out for the rest of the game with a wrist injury.

The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec previously reported the Ravens planned to activate Moore to the 53-man roster from the practice squad.

Bateman, who recorded no receptions after one was called back Sunday against the Colts, and tight end Mark Andrews, who tied for the team lead with six targets in Week 1, could see an uptick in targets should Flowers remained sidelined this weekend.

Moore and Wester could also receive more usage as the Ravens brace to spend at least the next month without Lane.

Whether Walker and Flowers ramp up to full participation in practice this week will provide a first indication as to what the Ravens' wide receiver depth chart will look like when Sunday's home opener kicks off at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins Jokes He Has 'In-N-Out Problem,' Reveals Favorite Cheat Meal After Joining Raiders
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins has become a frequent patron of In-N-Out since signing with the team.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins has become a frequent patron of In-N-Out since signing with the team.

The four-time Pro Bowler told reporters Wednesday he "can put down a lot of In-n-Out burgers" and jokingly referred to it as a "problem."

"That is a great cheat meal," he said. "And coming home from a win on Sunday night, I don't know if I can think of a better spot than that."

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

Cousins typically purchases two Double-Doubles with fries.

In-N-Out has supplanted Cook Out as Cousins' desired stop for a cheat meal.

His love for Cook Out goes back to at least his time on the Atlanta Falcons. The Netflix series Quarterback showed a clip of him going through a drive-thru as an employee was oblivious to his identity:

Cook Out is based predominantly in the Southeast. By heading to a team in Vegas, Cousins had to know he was entering In-N-Out territory. Talk to anybody who has lived on the West Coast for any period and they'll inevitably provide their strongly held opinions — positive or negative — on the fast food chain.

The 38-year-old could treat himself to something special after Week 1. The Raiders took down the Miami Dolphins 27-13, and Cousins went 21-of-30 for 160 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions in his Las Vegas debut.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Out vs. Cardinals with Glute Injury, Latest News on Timeline to Return to Seahawks
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have ruled out quarterback Sam Darnold for Week 2's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, though they do not intend to put him on injured reserve.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks have ruled out quarterback Sam Darnold for Week 2's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, though they do not intend to put him on injured reserve.

Darnold suffered what the team has described as a " very unique soft-tissue " injury to his right glute during the first series of Week 1's win over the New England Patriots.

That means Drew Lock will get the start. The veteran backup played well in relief duty in Week 1, throwing for 187 and a touchdown without any turnovers while rushing for 13 yards and taking one sack.

Jalen Milroe is currently slated to be the backup on Sunday, and head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters the plan was to stick with Lock and Milroe rather than add an external option.

Keeping Darnold off injured reserve is a good indication that the Seahawks believe the starter could return sooner rather than later. An IR stint would mean missing at least four games.

The 29-year-old Darnold had a fantastic debut season for the Seahawks in 2025, throwing for 4,048 yards, 25 touchdowns and 14 interceptions during the regular season. He was even better in the playoffs, throwing for 672 yards and five touchdowns with zero interceptions while leading the team to a Super Bowl title.

The 2026 season hasn't gotten off to an ideal start, but it doesn't sound as though his time on the sidelines will be a lengthy one.

articles.title: Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris Reportedly Can't Return to NFL in 2026 After LSU Roster Drama
articles.summary: After attempting to return to LSU after spending time in NFL training camps this summer, tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris reportedly won't be allowed to jump back to the pros this year.
articles.body:
After attempting to return to LSU after spending time in NFL training camps this summer, tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris reportedly won't be allowed to jump back to the pros this year.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , the NFL sent a memo to teams on Wednesday announcing that Wright and Harris "are ineligible to visit, try out with or be signed by NFL clubs during the 2026 NFL season." Pelissero added that the memo stated that this announcement "is not inclusive of all 2026 draft-eligible players who returned to college."

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

According to agent Drew Rosenhaus, Wright "is looking at his legal options right now and we will have more to say in the near future."

After going undrafted in April, Wright spent the offseason with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns, while Harris joined the New Orleans Saints. When both players were waived by their respective teams last month, they made a shocking attempt to commit to play at LSU this season after a court injunction granted a temporary restraining order allowing some players to return to college for one more season. Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin defended his pursuit of the former NFL players.

"At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they're either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country," Kiffin said at the time . "So we've made the decision to recruit them like probably most people are."

However, Wright and Harris were not added to LSU's roster for the team's season opener against Clemson. Before the Tigers' Week 2 matchup against Louisiana Tech, they added cornerback Aidan Anding and defensive end Gabriel Reliford to complete their 105-man roster, putting an end to their efforts to add Wright and Harris. ESPN's Max Olson reported that attorney Ryan Downton, who represents Wright and Harris, said that the players are "considering their legal options."

Following Wednesday's memo from the NFL, Wright and Harris won't have anywhere to play in 2026. Pelissero noted that since they have already been draft-eligible, they will simply become free agents at the end of the season.

articles.title: NFL declares Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who were at center of LSU controversy, ineligible for 2026 season
articles.summary: It seems Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright won't be playing football anywhere in 2026.
articles.body:
It seems Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright won't be playing football anywhere in 2026 — at least not in the NFL or NCAA. The NFL sent a memo to teams Wednesday declaring Harris and Wright ineligible to visit, try out or sign with an NFL team during the 2026 season.

Per the NFL memo, concerning Harris and Wright:

"The following players who were eligible for the 2026 NFL Draft returned to college and participated with their college football team after the opening of NFL training camp, and therefore, they are ineligible to visit, tryout [sic] with, or be signed by NFL clubs during the 2026 season."

Harris, Wright now banished from college and NFL football

Harris, a defensive tackle, and Wright, a tight end, were at the center of the NCAA eligibility controversy at LSU in the preseason. Both players agreed to join Lane Kiffin's LSU roster after signing with NFL teams but not making rosters.

This set off a firestorm in the SEC and across the NCAA as LSU appeared intent on rostering both players in spite of SEC mandates that neither player was eligible. Amid the intense outside pressure, LSU opted to not include either player on its final roster.

Now Harris and Wright are ineligible to play in the NFL until the 2027 season.

Harris and Wright both played for Kiffin when Kiffin was the head coach at Ole Miss. Neither player was drafted to the NFL after the 2025 season, but both players signed with NFL teams ahead of training camps.

Wright signed with the Philadelphia Eagles before joining the Cleveland Browns for their training camp. He was waived by the Browns. Harris signed with the New Orleans Saints and was also waived.

After being released, both players attempted to rejoin the NCAA with Kiffin at LSU, ultimately setting up a showdown with LSU against the SEC and NCAA regarding their eligibility.

Baton Rouge judge's ruling set off firestorm at LSU

They both initially joined LSU after a court ruling by Baton Rouge-based District Court Judge William Jorden granted more than 40 former NCAA athletes from the 2022 recruiting class a fifth year of eligibility in conflict with an NCAA ruling restricting them. The NCAA recently passed its "five in five" model granting athletes five years of eligibility, but it did not apply to the 2022 recruiting class.

Jorden's ruling led to a wave of players who had signed pro contracts attempting to return to college on NIL deals, several with LSU. The SEC, Big Ten, Big 12 and ACC responded with their own resolutions barring players who had been drafted by pro teams or signed pro contracts from playing for their programs.

Kiffin welcomed Wright and Harris in defiance of the SEC resolution, escalating the situation to the point that the SEC was considering expelling LSU from the conference .

LSU ultimately left Harris and Wright off its final roster amid the conflict. The end result for Wright and Harris is that they find themselves in football limbo.

articles.title: Bengals' Joe Burrow says he's dealing with back tightness, 'normal game day soreness' but will play in Week 2
articles.summary: Joe Burrow called it "ridiculous" to suggest he won't play in Week 2.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has proven to be an MVP-caliber talent, but only in the seasons in which he's been able to stay on the field. Over his career, Burrow has missed significant time with knee, wrist and foot injuries.

So the alarm bells were raised Wednesday, when Burrow didn't do much throwing during the open portion of Bengals' practice. But Burrow calmed fears after practice, saying he's dealing with back tightness and "normal game day soreness." He then made it clear that he'll play against the Houston Texans in Week 2.

Burrow went so far as to say it was "ridiculous" to suggest he wouldn't take the field Sunday.

Burrow, however, would not commit to how much he would take part in practices the rest of the week.

It's unclear exactly when Burrow sustained the injury, though he did take a big hit near his throwing shoulder on a scramble at the end of the first half Sunday.

Burrow said Wednesday he couldn't think of a particular play in which he sustained his injury. He said he felt his back tightness after Sunday's game and was comfortable with taking a big hit on a scramble late in the second quarter because it kept the team's drive alive.

Burrow did not miss any snaps after that play, and completed 11-of-15 passes for 121 yards in the second half of the Bengals' 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 1. Burrow also threw a pick-6 in the second half, though did not appear limited as the Bengals closed out the win.

He finished the contest 25 of 35, with 254 passing yards. He threw one touchdown and one interception in the victory.

Given his injury history — Burrow missed six games as a rookie after tearing his ACL, missed six games with a wrist injury in 2023 and was limited to just eight games last season with a foot injury — the fact that Burrow is already dealing with an ailment should be a cause for concern among fans.

In the three seasons in which Burrow has played every game, he's won two Comeback Player of the Year awards, made two Pro Bowls and finished fourth in the MVP voting twice.

While it's concerning that Burrow is already battling an ailment, his back tightness doesn't sound too serious. The Texans' defense should provide a significant challenge to Burrow and the rest of the Bengals' offense in Week 2, so it's in his best interest to get his body right before taking the field Sunday.

articles.title: Bengals' Joe Burrow Says It's 'Ridiculous' to Think He'll Miss Texans Game with Back Tightness
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow left no doubt as to his status for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans as he's experiencing some back tightness.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow left no doubt as to his status for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans as he's experiencing some back tightness.

Burrow told reporters it would be "ridiculous" to assume he won't suit up.

The Bengals deviated from their usual script a bit in their 33-27 Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Defense carried the day as Cincy held the Bucs to 282 yards and forced four turnovers. Burrow, meanwhile, was solid without lighting it up. He went 25-of-35 for 254 yards, one touchdown and an interception.

The collective performance was an encouraging sign after the front office invested heavily in overhauling its defense. The unit has to show improvement compared to recent years in order to end the Bengals' playoff drought.

Things won't get any easier in Week 2 with a road trip to Houston on tap.

C.J. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns while David Montgomery and Woody Marks combined for 102 yards on the ground in a 36-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Maybe the Cincinnati defense will have more success in limiting Stroud's effectiveness. In the event that doesn't happen, a lot will be thrust onto Burrow's shoulders in what has been a familiar refrain with this team.

Needless to say, the Bengals will be in trouble if his back issue is serious enough to sideline him.

articles.title: With De'Zhaun Stribling out 10 weeks, 49ers must adapt their passing game
articles.summary: The loss of De'Zhaun Stribling might not sink the 49ers' offense, but it could present some limitations until he returns much farther down the line.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling has landed on injured reserve, and the news on his left ankle injury he suffered in the Niners' Week 1 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia is worse than initially feared.

Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stribling underwent surgery to repair the deltoid ligament sprain in his left ankle and is expected to miss around 10 weeks. That's a ligament on the inside of the foot and far less common than sprains to the exterior ligaments in ankles.

Initially, the team hoped that Stribling's injury could heal without surgery and that he could return following a four-week IR stint. Now he will miss more than half of his rookie season, a cruel blow for a team that has been crippled by injuries the past few years.

The second-round draft pick (33rd overall selection) from April was a standout player in training camp and the preseason, recording 11 catches for 109 yards in the first two exhibition games. Stribling didn't catch any passes in the opener but was leading the team in routes run when he left the game with the ankle injury.

The Niners were as impressive as almost any team in Week 1, yet the injury bug continues to gnaw at them, also losing tight end Jake Tonges to a season-ending knee injury against the Rams.

Can they withstand Stribling's injury and stay competitive with the NFC heavyweights while he's out? Let's investigate.

Filling the Stribling vacancy in the meantime

Stribling missing around 10 weeks significantly changes the outlook for the Niners' passing game. If he remains on pace with his rehabilitation, 10 weeks out would put him on track to return for the 49ers' second game against the Seahawks, in Week 12. He still could face each division opponent once more and have the final tranche of games to potentially ramp up for the postseason, but there's no guarantee he'll return in peak form if he does.

The 49ers were genuinely excited for Stribling and appeared to have big plans for him this season. Losing the 6-foot-2, sub-4.4-running Stribling takes an element away from San Francisco 's offense that might not be easily replicable.

The first order of business for replacing Stribling was signing KhaDarel Hodge off the practice squad to the team's 53-man roster. Hodge was elevated from the practice squad in Week 1, playing one snap on offense and 12 more on special teams.

The other receivers who played in the opener are the three the 49ers are most likely to lean on during Stribling's absence: Mike Evans , Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel Sr. All three caught TD passes in the opener. Jacob Cowing also received five offensive snaps in the opener and served as the team's primary punt returner.

Evans showed in the opener why the Niners went after him this offseason despite being in the autumn of his career. His red-zone TD was classic Evans — and he's the kind of receiver they haven't had in recent years. Signing Evans feels even smarter now, and he figures to be the head honcho among the receivers.

Samuel showed why the 49ers brought him back, too, with 60 scrimmage yards on seven touches. He figures to resume his jack-of-all-trades role, lining up in the slot, out wide or even in the backfield.

Robinson, whose role increased as last season wore on and who had a big impact on the wild-card upset over the Philadelphia Eagles , has some big-play splash to help replace what they're missing with Stribling out.

The 49ers might lack a more vertical threat among them, outside of Robinson, which is a worry. But they might be able to creatively forge a few deep shots for Robinson and Cowing (and perhaps Hodge and Watkins, depending on their roles) to keep the shape of the offense similar.

Remember: The Niners lost Ricky Pearsall to a season-ending injury this offseason. Had he been healthy, perhaps losing Stribling wouldn't feel so tough right now.

Christian Kirk , who landed on short-term IR with a calf injury he suffered on the first day of training camp, is eligible to practice after the Week 2 game and can return as early as Week 5. Kirk is more of a professional slot weapon than a true outside threat, but he can help this team out.

Robinson's reliability, missing only a handful of games over his decade-long career, is one of his hallmarks. Good health was one of Evans' long-time calling cards, but he did miss more than half the season with injury in 2025 and turned 33 in August, creeping up on 200 career games. Samuel and Kirk have been injury-riddled, to varying degrees, throughout their careers. There are some questions here.

Losing Stribling fundamentally changes the makeup of the Niners' passing game, taking away a major slant-fade type of threat. It also limits what Brock Purdy and Shanahan can do to attack the intermediate and deeper parts of the field. It's hard to call the situation desperate, but it's concerning, even if there's still a chance Stribling contributes this season.

It will be interesting to see how the Niners compensate without the talented rookie, but they have a lot of arrows in their quiver, from Christian McCaffrey to George Kittle to Shanahan himself, plus Purdy's ability to extend plays and create on the move.

Collectively, they can survive in the short term. Longer term might be more of a stretch.

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr. Gives Injury Update Ahead of Falcons-Panthers After Missing Week 1 Amid Knee Issue
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. provided an update on the health of his knee after he was inactive during the team's Week 1 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. provided an update on the health of his knee after he was inactive during the team's Week 1 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

"I'm still working toward [playing]," Penix said Wednesday, according to ESPN's Marc Raimondi . "We're working right now. I'm close. I know I've been saying that."

The signal-caller also explained that he wants to suit up, but still has more steps to take in his recovery.

"I'm dying to be out there," Penix said, per Raimondi . "At the same time, I have to think about how I feel."

Penix suffered a torn ACL in Week 11 of the 2025 season before Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes sustained a torn ACL in Week 15 of last year.

While Mahomes was able to start for the Chiefs to open his 2026 campaign, Penix noted that he's underwent more knee procedures than the two-time MVP.

Penix didn't close the door on being active in Week 2, but is taking a day-to-day approach with his health.

"I've gotta focus on what I can do to get better every day," Penix said, per Raimondi .

He also confirmed that he'll be the one to determine when he's available this season.

Penix was in a positional battle with Tua Tagovailoa for Atlanta's starting quarterback role in training camp, but wasn't cleared to practice fully until Aug. 22.

Tagovailoa earned the first-string job before he also ended up missing the Falcons' season-opening defeat against the Steelers due to an oblique injury , as Cooper Rush ultimately started under center.

Rush finished 12-of-22 for 143 yards and one touchdown to go along with a pair of interceptions in the 20-13 loss.

On Monday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that the Falcons "would like Michael Penix to be their starting quarterback when he is healthy."

The original return timeframe for Penix was Week 2 or Week 3, per Rapoport.

The former first-round pick was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice on Atlanta's injury report , while Tagovailoa did not participate due to the oblique issue.

Penix previously started nine games for the Falcons last season, completing 60.1 percent of his throws for 1,982 yards and nine touchdowns compared to three interceptions.

Atlanta will face the Carolina Panthers in Week 2. Carolina struggled defensively during a season-opening loss to the Chicago Bears, allowing 59 points and 552 total yards.

The Falcons and Panthers are set to clash on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: NFL reiterates in memo that 2 players who left the pros to play at LSU also can’t play in the league this year
articles.summary: The NFL sent a memo reiterating that Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris cannot play in the league this season after attempting a college comeback at LSU.
articles.body: The two football players at the center of the debate over former professional players returning to the college game remain in limbo after the NFL notified teams they are ineligible to play this season. In a memo sent to top front-office staff and head coaches around the league on Wednesday, the NFL Player Personnel Department said defensive tackle Zxavian Harris and tight end Dae’Quan Wright are ineligible for the remainder of the 2026 campaign. This comes after the NFL last month said players who return to college would forfeit their eligibility to play in the league this season. Harris and Wright were “eligible for the 2026 NFL Draft, returned to college and participated with their college football team after the opening of NFL training camp, and therefore they are ineligible to visit, tryout with, or be signed by NFL clubs during the 2026 NFL season,” the memo stated. Harris and Wright both spent time in NFL training camps over the summer as undrafted free agents before being waived. Recent court decisions briefly opened their paths to returning to the college ranks, prompting both players to enroll at Louisiana State University (LSU) with hopes of playing for head coach Lane Kiffin and the Tigers this season. A Louisiana court ruled that the school could allow Wright and Harris to play on the Tigers’ football team despite both players having spent time in NFL training camps over the summer. Both players are now enrolled at LSU but Kiffin left them off his roster for the season-opening blowout win over Clemson. Kiffin initially held two roster spots open, signaling that Wright and Harris could fill them at a later date. That move set in motion a chaotic sequence of events heading into the season’s second week. The players’ presence with the team, and Kiffin’s intent to put them on his active roster, started a massive showdown between the school and the Southeastern Conference, which had passed a rule banning former professional players from competing for member schools. The standoff escalated to the point where the SEC threatened severe sanctions, including potential expulsion from the conference. LSU eventually filled the roster spots with two other players, defusing the immediate standoff and suspending discussions regarding the conference penalizing out one of its founding members. However, the fallout now deepens for Wright and Harris, who were under the impression that they would be able to play college ball again this year and improve their standing with NFL teams after failing to catch on this year. With the SEC blocking their return to college and the NFL closing its doors for the year, both players remain stranded – unable to play at either level in 2026.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson names NFL legend he patterned his game after
articles.summary: Bijan Robinson finished Week 1 as the Atlanta Falcons‘ leading receiver, and Cooper Rush did not have to look very far when he needed an easy answer against...
articles.body:
Bijan Robinson finished Week 1 as the Atlanta Falcons ' leading receiver, and Cooper Rush did not have to look very far when he needed an easy answer against the Pittsburgh Steelers .

Robinson was targeted 10 times in Atlanta 's 20-13 loss, catching eight passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. He had seven catches for 66 yards by halftime, including a 23-yard touchdown on a screen, while the rest of the Falcons' passing game struggled to find much rhythm.

He still handled his usual work on the ground, carrying 21 times for 83 yards. That left Robinson with 173 of Atlanta's 263 yards from scrimmage, or 65.8% of the offense's total. According to NFL, that was the largest share by any player in a season opener since Eric Dickerson accounted for 66.6% of the Rams' scrimmage yards in 1986.

Robinson also finished the opening week with more receiving yards than any running back in the league. Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving was next with 48.

Bijan Robinson has been catching the football for a long time

Atlanta using Robinson this way did not just start on Sunday.

He caught 79 passes for 820 yards and four touchdowns last season while also rushing for 1,478 yards. No player in NFL history had previously finished a season with at least 1,400 rushing yards and 810 receiving yards.

Robinson told DJ Siddiqi in an exclusive interview with Covers that catching the football has never felt foreign to him.

"Obviously running the football is the main priority, but then being an effective player in the pass game too. I've always conquered football my whole life. I played 7-on-7 flag my whole life. That's just something that God gifted me to do, and route-running and catching footballs, it's a natural thing that I love to do.

"They wanted to exploit it more here when I got to the NFL. That's what I've been doing, man. It's something that I appreciate, because you become a threat all over the field and become a guy that you have to watch for no matter where I line up and have an impact in that way. I want to continue to keep helping my team through that, and just continue to get better."

When Robinson was asked which back he patterned his game after, he went straight to Marshall Faulk.

"I looked up to Marshall Faulk," Robinson said. "Obviously, he's the prototype who I look up to in running style and catching the football."

Faulk once caught 87 passes for 1,048 yards in 1999 and finished his Hall of Fame career with 767 receptions for 6,875 yards. Robinson also named Barry Sanders, LaDainian Tomlinson and Adrian Peterson among the backs he watched and borrowed from.

Kevin Stefanski said after the Pittsburgh game that Atlanta will continue leaning on Robinson. The Falcons get Carolina at home Sunday, and after 29 touches in the opener, that workload could again include plenty of routes along with the carries.

articles.title: Week 2 NFL Power Rankings: Shakeup in the top five after Week 1
articles.summary: After Week 1, filled with high-scoring games and a shocking upset, here are the Week 2 power rankings, including a new team in the No. 1 spot.
articles.body:
The NFL has finally returned. After Week 1, there are a lot of things we can take away. The Baltimore Ravens looked dominant on both sides of the ball, while Josh Allen looks like he could win the MVP again. Chicago 's offense is electric, but they still need a defense. Seattle is certainly a Super Bowl contender, but are the Rams , especially with Myles Garrett out for the next four weeks? Let's take a look at our power rankings as we prepare for Week 2.

The Buffalo Bills offense took an elite Houston Texans defense and made them look sloppy, putting up 36 points and never turning the ball over. On the other side of the ball, the Bills may have allowed Houston to score 31 points, but they came up big in the end with a strip-sack on Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud. Josh Allen had four total touchdowns in this game and is clearly benefiting from the Bills acquiring wide receiver DJ Moore in the offseason.

Derrick Henry is the best running back in the NFL, and he proved it in the opener with 144 rushing yards and three touchdowns. His age doesn't matter, and he is a perfect complement to quarterback Lamar Jackson . Declan Doyle had a good debut as the offensive coordinator for the Ravens. Defensively, they dominated the Indianapolis Colts ' offense and held Jonathan Taylor to under 100 yards, which is really an accomplishment when it comes to Taylor. Maybe this is the Ravens team that finally makes it back to the Super Bowl.

Watching this game, I was really impressed with San Francisco's defense. While I believe jet lag played a role in how sluggish the Los Angeles Rams looked, they still could not get anything going on the ground or through the air. The reigning MVP, Matthew Stafford , finished the game with only 155 passing yards, which was his lowest total since playing the Seattle Seahawks last year. On the offense, Brock Purdy had three passing touchdowns. Mike Evans looked like he is still in his prime, and the 49ers are definitely glad to have Deebo Samuel back.

If this were a ranking of offenses, Chicago would be on top after exploding for 59 points, powered by Caleb Williams four total touchdowns - two on the ground and two through the air - as well as running back D'Andre Swift's three touchdowns. This offense was on another level, but their defense still needs a lot of work. They allowed Panthers receiver Jalen Coker to put up 138 receiving yards and two touchdowns, and quarterback Bryce Young tied his career-high for passing touchdowns. They have a lot of things to fix defensively if they want to get back to the Super Bowl for the first time since 2006.

Seattle still runs through their defense, and it certainly helps to have Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the other side of the ball. The Seahawks would be ranked higher if Sam Darnold had not gotten injured, and he has already been ruled out for Seattle's next game against the Arizona Cardinals . Jadarian Price has had some good runs, but their run game isn't as strong as it was with Kenneth Walker III. Still, the reigning Super Bowl champions cannot be counted out with their elite defense.

articles.title: Kevin Byard hopes to add Aaron Rodgers to his interception collection
articles.summary: The Patriots safety has intercepted a lot of great quarterbacks in his career. Rodgers is not yet among them.
articles.body:
Kevin Byard has made a habit out of intercepting opposing quarterbacks. Since entering the NFL as a third-round draft pick in 2016, he has picked off 37 passes and twice led the league in interceptions.

A total of 28 different QBs fell victim to his ball-hawking skills, including some of the best in the league today. One prominent name, however, is missing: Aaron Rodgers .

On Sunday, Byard will have a chance to add the current Pittsburgh Steelers passer to the list. He is very much looking forward to doing so.

"Definitely looking to get my first interception against Aaron Rodgers this week," the 33-year-old explained at his locker on Wednesday. "But, no, I think it's going to be fun, and really I just want to win. I don't care if I don't get an interception. If we just get some turnovers on defense, I'll be more than happy. But it's definitely something that's on my mind."

Despite Byard and Rodgers being among the most experienced players in the NFL right now, they only have crossed paths three times so far. All of those meetings came when the former was with the Titans and the latter with the Packers, and none of it included Byard getting his hands on a pass.

If this changes this week, Rodgers would be joining a list filled with prominent names.

"Got [Patrick] Mahomes . Got Josh Allen a couple of times. Dak Prescott a few times," Byard recalled. "It's countless, honestly. It's almost too much to count at this point. But I would say those are probably the top two, Josh Allen and Mahomes. I think I got Lamar [Jackson] too, so I got a lot of guys."

Byard added that he has each of the footballs he picked off lying around in his attic, even though he does not plan to change their whereabouts until after his retirement. Turning them into a leather chair was mentioned as one possible way to repurpose the balls.

How big that theoretical chair will end up being remains to be seen, and also if it will ultimately end up having that long-awaited connection to Aaron Rodgers.
